baseline_ref.window: fixed: the FAA issues a ground stop for every airport, a whole airline, an airline's request at 2 or more airports within 2 h, or an airport's equipment or communications outage (BO-IND-17); kept 24 h after it ends

sources.descriptor: The FAA's own advisory ordering the ground stop: what it stopped, the condition it names and its effective times. It says what the FAA did, not why a system failed.
sources.licence: US Government work (Federal Aviation Administration), public domain; credited to the FAA's Air Traffic Control System Command Center
sources.publisher: Federal Aviation Administration, Air Traffic Control System Command Center (ATCSCC)
sources.title: ATCSCC advisories database: ground stops

properties.summary: The FAA's Command Center issued a ground stop at ORD for EQUIPMENT / OUTAGE, from 21:21 UTC 24 Nov 2026, to 23:15 UTC 24 Nov 2026 (the last effective time the FAA gave; no cancellation was read). Condition the FAA names: EQUIPMENT / OUTAGE. Advisories: 53, 54. Reported by the FAA; Blackout does not assess why the system failed. A ground stop is the FAA's tool: an airline outage that only holds flights at the gate, with no stop requested, does not appear here.
properties.title: FAA ground stop at ORD: EQUIPMENT / OUTAGE (ended)
